draft.emotion: refreshing and satisfying, like quenching a real thirst
notes: In Brazil, 'tomar' is very commonly used instead of 'beber' when naming the beverage (e.g., 'tomar água', 'tomar café').
When used without an object, 'beber' usually means to drink alcohol.

draftBefore.emotion: refreshing and satisfying, like quenching a real thirst
notes: Use 'beber' for consuming liquids in general. In Brazil, 'tomar' is also very common for drinking water, coffee, or soft drinks, often interchangeable with 'beber'.
If you want to say 'to drink alcohol' specifically, you can also use 'beber' or the more informal 'tomar uma'.
